title: A continuous real function attains its minimum on a nonempty compact set
statement: Let $T$ be a topological space and let $C\subseteq T$ be nonempty and compact in its subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Here compact means that every cover by open sets admits a finite subcover. Let $f:T\to\mathbf R$ be continuous on $C$, meaning that its restriction to that subspace is continuous. Then there exists $c_0\in C$ such that $f(c_0)\leq f(c)$ for every $c\in C$.
